Field notes · Session planning

Your graduation photo checklist

Caps, gowns, locations, and the little details that make it yours.

Graduation photographs mark more than the end of a semester. They’re a way to remember the work that got you here and the person you’ve become. A little preparation makes room to enjoy the occasion.

Start with when you need the images.

If you want photographs for announcements, invitations, or a celebration, work backward from that date. Tell me your deadline before booking so we can agree on a realistic session and delivery schedule.

Pack a small session bag.

  • Your cap and gown, steamed or neatly pressed.
  • Any cords, stole, tassel, or other graduation details.
  • An outfit you feel good wearing without the gown.
  • Comfortable shoes for moving between spots.
  • Water, a comb or brush, and a few pins for the cap.
  • A meaningful prop if there’s something you want to include.

Choose a place with a reason.

A campus can tell one part of your story; a favorite outdoor setting can tell another. For BYU and UVU graduates, we can discuss a campus-inspired session or a different setting in Provo or Orem. Any location access or photography requirements should be checked before finalizing the plan.

Make time for the individual.

Plan for photographs in the gown and photographs without it. We can create a classic portrait, a little movement, and something that speaks to your personality. You don’t need to know a collection of poses beforehand.

Avoid bringing loose confetti into outdoor spaces. A cap in the air, a big laugh, or a little movement makes a celebration without leaving anything behind.

Bring someone who makes you comfortable.

A friend or family member can help carry your things and bring a little extra confidence. If they’re also joining the photographs, mention that in your inquiry so we can plan the time.
